correctness.rationale: The substitution y=e^t−1 and Stirling expansion are formally coefficientwise finite and give integral coefficients. Modulo 2^r, terms of factorial index at least 2r vanish, and for n≥r all even bases of the fixed finite inclusion–exclusion sum vanish. The modulo-32 cycle 31,17,31,1 repeats on n≥5 via the eighth powers of the odd bases; independently multiplying the truncated exponential series in integer derivative coordinates reproduced this cycle and passed 459 half-shift tests. For odd j, writing j²=1+8u gives ν₂(binomial(2^{s−1},k)·8^k)≥s−1−ν₂(k)+3k≥s+4 for k≥2 when the binomial is nonzero. This proves j^{2^s}−1≡2^{s−1}(j²−1) modulo 2^{s+4}, including s=1. Applied to the fixed odd bases, this lifts the base defect for every n≥r and r=s+4. Parity is preserved by the half-shift, so applying it twice gives a period; its half fails on all sufficiently large even n. The least eventual period divides any period by Euclidean differences. Reduction of the base cycle gives the parity alternation modulo 4, 8 and 16 and the constant tail modulo 2.
residual_risks: The separate finite computation does not establish the general lifting; the proof does. No least preperiod is asserted or audited.
